samples_reviewed.question_text: Start at 80. Count up 3 more. You land on 93. True or False?
The dot is at 64 and it moves forward 7 numbers. Starting from 64, just count up 7 numbers. Which number will the dot land on?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The counting-up model is genuinely enacted: each item starts at a two-digit number and moves forward by a one-digit amount, and the number-line items make that hop explicit by asking where the dot lands.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Hops that stay inside a ten and hops that cross one both occur in quantity, and starting points are spread from the thirties to the nineties rather than clustering at round numbers.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: A single one-digit hop from a stated two-digit start is exactly the load this competency is written for, and the stems stay to one or two short sentences.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Five presentations appear, which is good, but all three true-or-false items are keyed False. That variant therefore rewards answering False without ever counting up, which defeats the point of including it.

competency_alignment.rationale: The difficulty ramp raises the starting number while holding the hop at a single digit, which is the right axis: the challenge in counting up is where you start, not how far you go.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: One item starts at 94 and counts up 7, landing on 101. That carries the illustration out of the two-digit territory the competency frames, and on a number-line model the crossing of a hundred is a distinctly different picture from the rest of the set.
